sources.title: Agency A direction notice
sources.text: Agency A issued a binding direction on 17 August 2040. Board B must use the higher of the calculated grade and the centre estimate for Cohort A candidates with a centre estimate. Candidates without a centre estimate fall outside this route. Agency A directs the grading rule; this notice does not show Agency A operating Board B's software.

sources.title: Board B issue bulletin
sources.text: Board B reports that it issued corrected records on 19 August 2040 for Cohort A candidates covered by Agency A's direction. This is Board B's account of issuance. The bulletin contains no recipient acknowledgements and does not establish that any named candidate received a corrected record.

sources.title: Agency A advice-panel record
sources.text: A formal technical advice panel existed before 17 August 2040 and included Agency A board members. This record does not identify which underlying material those members accessed before the grading direction.

sources.title: Agency A harm acknowledgement
sources.text: Agency A acknowledges that the grading process caused distress and uncertainty. It has no complete individual-outcome or remedy record. A changed grade or a corrected record does not, by itself, establish that all consequential harm was repaired.

qualifications.text: All actors, dates, sources and events in this packet are constructed. They are not new historical evidence about Ofqual.
Agency A's demonstrated role is regulatory direction. Its operation of Board B's software is not established.
The direction covers Cohort A candidates with a centre estimate. It excludes candidates without one.
A report of issuance alone does not establish recipient receipt. Any later signed receipts establish receipt only for the specifically named recipients.
Repair of every consequential harm remains unestablished, including when some corrected records have been received.
Actual access to underlying material before the direction remains unresolved. A formal advice route does not establish retrieval.

The fact that Board B reported issuance and the occurrence of issuance are different propositions. An equally admissible contrary account creates a conflict about occurrence without erasing the original report.
